blog/airbnb-revenue-projections/index.ht.description: Compare seller history, comparable rentals and monthly assumptions. Stress-test Airbnb revenue projections against operating costs and debt before buying.
blog/airbnb-revenue-projections/index.ht.heading: Use your projections to prepare an acquisition discussion
blog/airbnb-revenue-projections/index.ht.body:
Bring the listing, seller revenue records, comparable-property sources, monthly assumptions and expense quotes. Keep the downside case visible when discussing the purchase price. Review the revenue evidence checklist and BNB Accelerator’s acquisition scope and fees.

blog/switching-property-managers/index.h.title: Switch Airbnb Property Managers: Bookings & Handoff
blog/switching-property-managers/index.h.description: Plan an Airbnb property-manager change around the contract, future reservations, listing control, guest communication and operating handoff.
blog/switching-property-managers/index.h.heading: Changing managers or buying a property with bookings?
blog/switching-property-managers/index.h.body: Replacing a manager for a property you already own is a different decision from taking ownership of a seller’s rental. If you are buying, review future reservations at closing and document the responsibilities of the seller, manager and buyer. BNB Accelerator’s service is acquisition support; confirm any post-closing coordination in writing rather than assuming ongoing property management is included.

blog/future-reservations-at-closing/inde.heading: Already own the property and changing managers?
blog/future-reservations-at-closing/inde.body: Use the property-manager transition guide for contract notice, listing control and operating handoff. A manager change and a property purchase have different parties and responsibilities; confirm what happens to existing reservations with the professionals and platform involved.

short-term-rental-investment-service/ind.title: Short-Term Rental Acquisition Service | BNB Accelerator
short-term-rental-investment-service/ind.description: Compare short-term rental acquisition support for your first purchase, including property screening, underwriting, diligence and the launch handoff.
short-term-rental-investment-service/ind.heading: What to expect from a short-term rental acquisition service
short-term-rental-investment-service/ind.body:
Ask who screens listings, who checks the income evidence and who coordinates the handoff after closing. Request a sample screening memo, the assumptions behind its downside case and a written list of deliverables. Separately confirm who represents you in the transaction and which licensed professionals will provide financing, insurance and legal advice.

Review fees and scope, compare the types of Airbnb investment companies, or use the buyer roadmap to see what you can handle yourself.

airbnb-investment-company/index.html.title: How to Choose an Airbnb Investment Company
airbnb-investment-company/index.html.description: Compare Airbnb investment companies, buyer agents and acquisition consultants by fee structure, representation, diligence and handoff responsibilities.
airbnb-investment-company/index.html.heading: Compare a buyer agent, an investment consultant and a turnkey provider
airbnb-investment-company/index.html.body:
Ask each provider for the same four items: a sample property shortlist, a written fee schedule, an example downside analysis and a responsibility chart through launch. Confirm who represents you, who gets paid at closing, and which work is referred to a third party. If you are comparing a turnkey Airbnb investment with buying and furnishing a property yourself, price both routes through the first bookable night, including carrying costs and reserves.

See BNB Accelerator’s acquisition support and the written scope and fees.

buy-a-short-term-rental/index.html.title: How to Buy a Short-Term Rental | First-Time Buyer Roadmap
buy-a-short-term-rental/index.html.description: Learn how to buy a short-term rental. Screen the address, verify seller income and permits, compare loans and use the due diligence checklist.
buy-a-short-term-rental/index.html.heading: A due diligence checklist for buying a short-term rental
buy-a-short-term-rental/index.html.body:
1. Confirm permission at the address. Ask the local authority whether the current short-term rental permit transfers, whether a new owner must reapply and whether any cap or waiting list applies. Review the association documents separately.
  2. Reconcile the seller’s income. Compare platform payouts, booking calendars, refunds and operating statements over the same dates. Set aside any reservations you cannot confirm will transfer.
  3. Price the risks before contingency deadlines. Get an insurance quote for the intended use, written financing terms and repair estimates. Update the downside case and record what would cause you to reprice or walk away.

Track evidence and deadlines in the due diligence document tracker. For help finding and evaluating properties, review the acquisition service.

financing/index.html.title: Short-Term Rental Financing: DSCR vs. Conventional Loans
financing/index.html.description: Compare vacation rental financing, DSCR and conventional loans. Check eligible income, reserves, lender restrictions and closing costs before making an offer.
financing/index.html.heading: Compare vacation rental financing on the same purchase
financing/index.html.body:
Ask each lender for a written scenario using the same address, purchase price and down payment. Compare the lender’s qualifying income method, payment, points, prepayment terms, reserves and cash due at closing. Ask a DSCR lender whether it accepts projected short-term rental income and how it treats a property with limited operating history.

Read the short-term rental DSCR loan guide and the DSCR versus conventional comparison. Update your acquisition budget when you receive actual terms.

tools/index.html.title: Airbnb Investment Calculators & Short-Term Rental Tools
tools/index.html.description: Use Airbnb revenue and short-term rental cash flow tools, a purchase budget worksheet and a downside calculator to check an investment before making an offer.
tools/index.html.heading: Build an Airbnb investment pro forma from evidence you can check
tools/index.html.body:
1. Estimate monthly room revenue with the short-term rental revenue calculator using rates and bookable nights for each season.
  2. Use the purchase budget calculator for cash at closing, furnishing and initial reserves. Track listing details, assumptions and open questions in the investment memo template.
  3. Run the downside calculator to see how weaker bookings or higher expenses affect cash flow. Keep operating profit, debt payments and replacement reserves visible as separate lines.

best-cities-airbnb-investment-2026/index.title: Best Cities for Airbnb Investment: How to Compare Markets
best-cities-airbnb-investment-2026/index.description: Compare cities for Airbnb and short-term rental investment using address-level rental rules, comparable listings, seasonal revenue, expenses and financing.
best-cities-airbnb-investment-2026/index.heading: Screen markets before you compare properties
best-cities-airbnb-investment-2026/index.body:
Start with three markets where you can confirm permission for your intended rental use. In each one, compare properties with similar bedroom count, amenities and access to demand drivers. Use monthly revenue assumptions and local quotes for insurance, cleaning and maintenance. A city can look attractive on gross revenue and still miss your cash-flow target after debt service and reserves.

Compare the market profiles, then run each candidate through the listing screening scorecard before commissioning deeper diligence.

underwriting/permit-transfer/index.html.heading: Build an address-level permit transfer record
underwriting/permit-transfer/index.html.body:
Keep a written record for the exact property. A seller’s permit number is useful evidence, but the relevant question is what the buyer must do after the ownership change.

  1. Record the address, parcel ID, permit ID, named holder, approved occupancy and expiration date. Note whether the permit covers the entire home or a specific unit.
  2. Ask the issuing office how it treats a sale, whether a new application or inspection is required and when the buyer can begin hosting. Record the response date and contact.
  3. Track association, lender and insurance restrictions in separate fields. If approval is unresolved, mark the expected first bookable night as unknown in your deal model.

Continue with the due diligence tracker and the HOA restrictions guide.

underwriting/insurance-quote/index.html.heading: Build a short-term rental insurance quote comparison
underwriting/insurance-quote/index.html.body:
Give every broker the same address, rental-use description, amenities, occupancy and target closing date so the quotes answer the same question.

  1. Record dwelling limit, liability limit, applicable deductibles, coverage start date and the endorsements or exclusions the broker identifies.
  2. Ask which underwriting requirements must be satisfied before coverage can start. Assign an owner to each open inspection, repair or documentation item.
  3. Store the quote separately from the evidence of coverage. Record when the lender needs proof and who will send it.

Continue with the quote, binder and policy comparison and the closing evidence tracker.

blog/str-buyer-agent-vs-acquisition-team.heading: Score a buyer agent and acquisition team on the same sample deal
blog/str-buyer-agent-vs-acquisition-team.body:
Send both providers one recent listing and ask what they would deliver before writing an offer. Comparing deliverables on the same example makes vague scope differences easier to spot.

  1. Request a screening memo that separates seller claims, verified inputs and open questions. Look for the evidence behind the revenue and expense lines.
  2. Ask who handles representation, writes the offer, checks dates and requests records. Confirm which counterparties pay each fee.
  3. Ask where responsibility ends at closing and who owns photography, furnishing and launch handoffs. Record any work requiring a separate agreement.

Continue with the investment company selection guide and the acquisition support scope.

blog/short-term-rental-market-analysis/i.heading: Run a comparable-property audit before picking a market
blog/short-term-rental-market-analysis/i.body:
Save comparable listings by month and record the reason for including each one. A popular city can contain several rental markets with different guest demand and operating constraints.

  1. Compare the same bedroom count, practical guest capacity and major amenities. Note whether competing listings are waterfront, walkable or otherwise materially different.
  2. Keep weekday, weekend and peak-event assumptions separate. Record the observation date for each listing and flag unavailable dates whose cause you cannot verify.
  3. Use local cost evidence for insurance, cleaning, utilities and maintenance. Rebuild the model with weaker shoulder seasons and compare the result across candidate properties.

Continue with the revenue calculator and the listing screening scorecard.

tools/str-revenue-calculator/index.html.heading: Build monthly Airbnb revenue scenarios
tools/str-revenue-calculator/index.html.body:
Model bookable nights and average rate by month. Keep guest fees, taxes collected and owner revenue in separate columns so the comparison survives a review of payout statements.

  1. Start with available nights after planned owner use, maintenance blocks and expected launch delays. Keep availability and booking assumptions separate.
  2. Use different rate and booking assumptions for peak and shoulder months. Note what records, comps or quotes support each input.
  3. Compare projected room revenue with the actual seller statements for the same months. Move debt service, operating expenses and reserves into a separate cash-flow model.

Continue with the revenue evidence checklist and the downside calculator.

tools/str-downside-calculator/index.html.heading: Stress-test short-term rental cash flow month by month
tools/str-downside-calculator/index.html.body:
An annual return can hide months when debt and carrying costs still come due. Build a monthly view using the same dates as the base case.

  1. Test three changes separately before combining them: launch delay, fewer booked nights and higher operating costs. Note the source and owner of each assumption.
  2. Compare the lowest monthly balance, the largest cumulative cash draw and the month when the property recovers. Include planned replacement spending on its expected date.
  3. Write down the purchase-price or reserve threshold you would revisit if the downside exceeds the cash you can commit.

Continue with the break-even occupancy guide and the acquisition budget worksheet.

buy-a-short-term-rental/investment-memo-.heading: Turn the investment memo into an Airbnb underwriting template
buy-a-short-term-rental/investment-memo-.body:
Use one versioned memo for each offer. Preserve the original case and record why each assumption changes as diligence comes in.

  1. Record purchase price, acquisition costs, financing terms, furnishing costs and reserves with a source beside each major input.
  2. Show monthly revenue, operating expenses and debt service in separate sections. Label the base and downside cases with their assumptions and dates.
  3. End with an unresolved-items table containing evidence needed, owner, deadline and the decision that changes if the evidence comes back differently.

Continue with the seller financials guide and the cash-flow stress test.

underwriting/seller-financials/index.htm.heading: Reconcile seller revenue through to cash received
underwriting/seller-financials/index.htm.body:
Pick a month with cancellations or refunds as well as a strong month. The two examples reveal whether the seller statements and payout records can be reconciled consistently.

  1. Match reservation references and stays to payout batches. Note payouts that settle in the next month and keep gross room charges separate from net cash.
  2. Identify refunds, adjustments and amounts that the listing platform collected for remittance. Record whether the seller used another channel or processed payments directly.
  3. Request the expense evidence for the same period. Flag undocumented line items and unusual owner blocks before using the figures as a forecast.

Continue with the revenue evidence checklist and the underwriting memo.

underwriting/hoa-restrictions/index.html.heading: Build a short-term rental HOA document checklist
underwriting/hoa-restrictions/index.html.body:
Review the documents for the exact association and unit. Keep informal explanations in your notes and retain the written provisions you used for the decision.

  1. Request recorded declarations and amendments, current rules, leasing forms and any applicable master-association records. Check for minimum stays, occupancy limits and approval procedures.
  2. Ask how the association tracks existing rentals and whether approvals attach to the owner or property. Record any cap, waiting list or enforcement matter and the effective date.
  3. Capture the cited document, page and section in your diligence tracker. Route conflicting provisions to the appropriate adviser before relying on them.

Continue with the permit transfer guide and the evidence tracker.

buy-a-short-term-rental/property-tour-ch.heading: Record rental setup constraints during the property tour
buy-a-short-term-rental/property-tour-ch.body:
Take room and exterior photos with permission and note the location of each concern. Connect the observations to costs and ownership decisions after the tour.

  1. Measure entry doors, landings and tight turns that can block furniture delivery. Photograph circuits, shutoffs and equipment labels where available for the relevant specialist.
  2. Walk the arrival route at the expected parking location. Identify potential problems with steps, signage, exterior lighting, noise and shared entrances.
  3. Separate observed conditions from suspected causes. Assign each open question to the correct inspection, quote or document request with a deadline.

Continue with the property screening scorecard and the final walkthrough checklist.

buy-a-short-term-rental/launch-handoff-c.heading: Prepare the first bookable night handoff
buy-a-short-term-rental/launch-handoff-c.body:
Schedule the handoff backward from a realistic first stay date. Give each prerequisite an owner and an acceptable evidence record.

  1. Confirm responsibility for keys, access codes, utilities, insurance evidence and required approvals. Establish a process for changing credentials at the handoff.
  2. Record furnishing delivery, photo readiness and cleaning dates. Note what will delay publication or opening the calendar.
  3. Run a trial arrival and turnover. Verify check-in directions, support contacts, inventory, and the route for anything found on the punch list.

Continue with the future reservations guide and the furnished inventory checklist.

underwriting/cash-needed-to-buy/index.ht.heading: Build a dated schedule of cash needed to buy
underwriting/cash-needed-to-buy/index.ht.body:
List costs by due date and mark which payments are credited at closing. This makes the cash schedule easier to compare with the lender’s estimate.

  1. Record earnest money, inspections, financing fees and funds due at closing. Keep any seller or lender credits tied to the estimate that supports them.
  2. Add the first month of utilities, property setup, delivery and any repairs required to open. Assign each estimate a source and an expected payment date.
  3. Include operating and lender reserve requirements as separate lines. Check whether the same available cash is serving two planned uses.

Continue with the purchase budget calculator and the closing costs and reserves guide.
